items.question: From whom must this teaching be carefully concealed in the mortal world?
premises: The teaching must be concealed
Concealment requires deliberate effort
The lowest of men are the context of concealment
items.inference: This teaching should be kept secret with effort from the lowest people in the mortal world.
items.plain_english: It must be carefully concealed in the mortal world from the lowest of men.

items.question: Under what condition may this teaching be given to a previously accomplished person?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient must be previously accomplished
The recipient must be tested for one year
items.inference: This teaching may be given only to a previously accomplished person who has been tested for one year.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is already accomplished and has been tested for one year.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the text emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: The text emerged from Candradvīpa
A chapter is being identified
The chapter is the fifth
items.inference: The fifth chapter of the work emerged from Candradvīpa concludes here.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the work that emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: Through whose grace has the determination of the Kaula doctrine become known?
premises: The speaker addresses the lord of Kaulas
Knowledge arose by that lord's grace
The Kaula determination is now known
items.inference: By the grace of the lord of Kaulas, the speaker has come to know the determination of the Kaula doctrine.
items.plain_english: O Lord of the Kaulas, by your grace I have come to know the determination of the Kaula doctrine.

items.question: What is the declared identity and essential nature of the individual soul?
premises: The soul has been declared in the teaching
Its identity is questioned
Its essential nature is questioned
items.inference: The verse asks both who the declared soul is and what its essential nature is.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared, and what is the true nature of the soul?

items.question: Into what does the soul dissolve, and what full explanation is requested?
premises: The soul undergoes dissolution
The locus of dissolution is questioned
The speaker requests a complete explanation
items.inference: The verse asks where the soul dissolves and requests that all of this be explained.
items.plain_english: And into what does it dissolve? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What supreme qualities define the true nature of that soul?
premises: The soul is identified as supreme
The soul is partless and eternal
The soul is free from disease and stain
items.inference: The soul is characterized as supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease, and stainless.
items.plain_english: He is supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease, and stainless.

items.question: How is the transcendent soul identified as haṃsa and as the individual of power?
premises: The soul is described as supremely transcendent
That soul is identified as haṃsa
That soul is identified as the individual of power
items.inference: The transcendent soul is identified as haṃsa, the individual associated with power.
uncertainties: The exact sense of śakti+pudgalaḥ is doctrinally compressed.
items.plain_english: That soul is supremely transcendent; indeed, he is the haṃsa, the individual of power.

items.question: How is the vital air described as present within all living beings?
premises: The air is filled with breath or wind
The air is situated in all beings
This presence is universal among living beings
items.inference: The breath-filled vital air is situated within all living beings.
uncertainties: Agreement of saṃsthitam with vāyuḥ is syntactically loose.
items.plain_english: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.

items.question: What is the soul called immediately upon leaving the body?
premises: The soul leaves the body
This departure is the decisive moment
At that moment it is called supreme Śiva
items.inference: Upon merely leaving the body, the soul is declared to be supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: As soon as it leaves the body, it is called supreme Śiva.

items.question: How is this teaching said to be received through traditional transmission?
premises: The teaching is heard in the ear
The goddess is addressed as recipient
The teaching comes down through tradition
items.inference: This teaching is heard in the ear as something transmitted through an unbroken tradition.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, it is heard in the ear, having come down through the succession of tradition.

items.question: What effect is attributed to merely hearing this knowledge, fair-faced goddess?
premises: The knowledge is merely heard
Hearing alone is emphasized
The fair-faced goddess is addressed
items.inference: Even mere hearing of this knowledge is presented as having significant effect.
uncertainties: The main predicate continues in the next verse.
items.plain_english: O fair-faced one, by merely hearing this knowledge...

items.question: What disciplined practice over six months leads to a state free from bondage?
premises: Practice is undertaken for six months
The practitioner engages in the ochre discipline
The goal is freedom from bondage
items.inference: One who practices for six months attains the ochre state free from bondage.
uncertainties: kāṣāyaṃ may refer to renunciant discipline rather than a robe.
items.plain_english: Whoever practices for six months attains the ochre state, free from bondage.

items.question: What two benefits result from sustained practice of this teaching?
premises: The practitioner becomes freed from all diseases
The practitioner gains union with yogis
These results follow the described practice
items.inference: The practice leads to freedom from all diseases and union with yogis.
items.plain_english: He becomes freed from all diseases and attains union with the yogis.

items.question: What teaching has now been fully communicated to Bhairavī regarding the soul?
premises: Bhairavī is addressed directly
The subject is the practice concerning the soul
This teaching has been told to her
items.inference: The practice concerning the soul has now been explained to Bhairavī.
items.plain_english: O Bhairavī, this practice concerning the soul has now been told to you.

items.question: To what kind of resolved recipient may this teaching properly be given?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient must be endowed with all states
The recipient must have a resolved mind
items.inference: This teaching should be given to a person of resolved mind who is endowed with all states.
uncertainties: The exact nuance of sarva+bhāva+upapannasya is interpretive.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is endowed with all states and whose mind is firmly resolved.

items.question: Why must the essential Kaula teaching originating from the yoginīs not be given indiscriminately?
premises: The Kaula essence is highly valued
It originates from the yoginīs
It must not be given
items.inference: The essential Kaula teaching, which originates from the yoginīs, must not be given out.
uncertainties: The syntactic relation of sambhavam is slightly compressed.
items.plain_english: The essential Kaula teaching, which originates from the yoginīs, must not be given.

items.question: What transformation of the body is claimed after the veil of ignorance is struck away?
premises: The body was struck by the veil of ignorance
A change is declared today
The body is now pure
items.inference: The speaker declares that today the body, once struck by ignorance, is now pure.
uncertainties: The contrast implies prior impurity though stated elliptically.
items.plain_english: Today my body, once struck by the veil of ignorance, is pure.

items.question: What auspicious knowledge about overcoming time does the speaker now wish to hear?
premises: The speaker expresses a present wish
The desired topic concerns time
The topic is the auspicious overcoming of time
items.inference: The speaker now wishes to hear about the auspicious overcoming of time.
uncertainties: vañcanaṃ can mean deception or outwitting; context favors overcoming.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear about the auspicious overcoming of time.

items.question: What assurance is given that death can truly be destroyed?
premises: The teacher promises to explain
There is said to be no doubt
Death is said to be destroyed
items.inference: The teacher assures without doubt that death can be destroyed and will explain how.
items.plain_english: I will tell you—there is no doubt—how death is destroyed.

items.question: What intense experience at the tip of nectar affects even the wise practitioner?
premises: The locus is the tip of nectar
There is contact with the essence of juice
Even a wise person experiences burning
items.inference: Even the wise one experiences a burning sensation at the tip of nectar through the essence of juice.
uncertainties: The physiological referent of amṛta+agraṃ is esoteric.
items.plain_english: Even the wise one feels a burning at the tip of nectar by the essence of the juice.

items.question: How should the practitioner draw in the vital air at the root of tongue and palate?
premises: The practice is located at the root of tongue and palate
The vital air is to be drawn in
The action must be done slowly
items.inference: The practitioner should slowly draw in the vital air at the root of the tongue and palate.
items.plain_english: Placing it at the root of the tongue and palate, one should slowly drink in the air.

items.question: What result follows from practicing this method continuously for one year?
premises: The practice is performed for one year
The practice becomes established
Old age and death are destroyed
items.inference: When this practice is maintained for one year, old age and death are destroyed.
items.plain_english: When practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: What immunity to venom is claimed for the accomplished practitioner’s body?
premises: The practitioner may be bitten by great serpents
Poison would normally enter the body
In this case poison does not enter
items.inference: Even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the practitioner's body.
items.plain_english: Even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the body.
